# Referee

Referee is research-integrity infrastructure for scholarly publishing. The platform turns technical evidence into transparent, machine-readable reliability signals that support structured triage and targeted expert review at high submission volume. Scoring is anchored to the public CRWE v2.1 flaw taxonomy (11 top-level categories, 300 structured checks).

Referee does not claim to replace expert peer review with a black box. It organizes checks into a structured evaluation record with explicit flaw categories, unresolved items, and auditable outputs.

## Key routes
- / — Homepage with product positioning, workflow, audience, differentiation, founder context, and demo call to action.
- /about — Mission, leadership profile, advisor profile, and collaboration/contact invitations.
- /blog — Index of published long-form articles.
- /blog/{slug} — Individual published blog articles.
- /faq — Frequently asked questions about model assumptions, incentives, adoption, AI, and governance concerns.
- /talks — Recorded presentations and interviews about the project.

## Homepage coverage
- Problem framing: rising submission volume, limited intake review capacity, fragmented integrity checks, and low auditability.
- Solution framing: structured screening and triage with transparent reliability scoring tied to evidence.
- Workflow model (CRWE-based):
  1) ingest paper evidence
  2) map checks to explicit weakness categories
  3) record checked vs unresolved items
  4) output machine-readable reliability signals for triage
- Value claims: better triage, better allocation of expert reviewer time, and clearer documentation of research risk.
- Target users: conference organizers, publishers/journals, and research organizations.
- Positioning: infrastructure layer that unifies checks into a reusable record rather than isolated one-off tools.
- Current demo scope: a curated scored-paper experience with the full evidence trail is available today; false positives and coverage depth are still being improved.
- Founder context: founder-owned technical architecture and implementation.

## About coverage
- Mission: improve transparency, efficiency, and accountability in research evaluation through reliability-oriented infrastructure.
- Leadership: Erik Schneider (Founder & Executive Director), background spanning finance, cybersecurity, insider risk, and computing.
- Advisor: Dr. Marcus Thomas (computational scientist; immuno-oncology/personalized cancer vaccine pipeline expertise).
- Collaboration posture: active outreach for additional qualified advisors and collaborators.

## Blog coverage (published posts)
- /blog/false-positives-false-negatives-and-the-real-calibration-problem
  - Title: False Positives, False Negatives, and the Real Calibration Problem
  - Focus: Any system that looks for research weaknesses will make mistakes. The real question is not whether errors occur, but whether they are visible, measurable, correctable, and tied to a versioned record rather than hidden inside prestige or private review.
- /blog/why-reliability-should-be-machine-readable
  - Title: Why Reliability Should Be Machine-Readable
  - Focus: Scholarship is searched, ranked, funded, cited, regulated, and reused by systems. Reliability information locked in prose cannot travel through those channels. Referee turns reliability into structured metadata that can move with the paper.
- /blog/defect-or-audit-gap-why-referee-forces-a-call-anyway
  - Title: Defect or Audit Gap? Why Referee Forces a Call Anyway
  - Focus: Research criticism usually collapses actual flaws and missing information into one vague complaint. Referee separates defects from audit gaps and then forces explicit yes/no calls on both. Ambiguity is preserved in the evidence record, not promoted into a third scoring state.
- /blog/from-pdf-to-provenance-how-a-referee-score-gets-made
  - Title: From PDF to Provenance: How a Referee Score Gets Made
  - Focus: Referee does not upload a paper to an AI model and ask for a vague review. It turns the paper into a structured record, runs narrow checks tied to the CRWE, records evidence, makes explicit yes/no calls, and preserves the provenance behind the score.
- /blog/what-a-referee-score-actually-measures
  - Title: What a Referee Score Actually Measures
  - Focus: The scholarly record already scores papers through prestige, reputation, and citation habits. Referee replaces those hidden scores with an explicit, versioned measure based on named research weaknesses, public evidence, and decomposable scoring.
- /blog/academic-collegiality-is-a-bug-not-a-feature
  - Title: Academic collegiality is a bug, not a feature (and it's largely not true)
  - Focus: critiques assumptions about collegial peer review and argues for more direct, democratized, adversarial criticism in research evaluation.
- /blog/gaming-referee
  - Title: Gaming Referee
  - Focus: living threat model describing how adversaries might game the system (collusion, sybils, flooding, corruption, etc.) and corresponding mitigations.
- /blog/no-ai-agents-no-scalability-in-research-validation
  - Title: No AI Agents, No Scalability in Research Validation
  - Focus: argues that scalable research validation requires specialized AI agents paired with validation controls and expert oversight.

## FAQ topic coverage
The /faq page (Objections and Principles; full text at /faq.md) has two groups.
- Principles:
  - Why Referee exists: replacing opaque trust with legible reliability metadata.
  - Why use a reliability score at all, versus prestige proxies.
  - Why the score is machine-readable.
  - Why review is decomposed into targeted checks.
  - The role experts still play.
  - Why many targeted reviews do not need a traditional academic referee.
- Objections:
  - Whether a single score is too reductive.
  - Whether one framework can work across disciplines.
  - Why Referee borrows from bug-bounty logic.
  - What prevents gaming.
  - How non-experts contribute without lowering quality.
  - AI errors, hallucinations and shallow understanding.
  - Relationship to PubPeer and other post-publication commentary.
  - How journals will react.
  - Anonymity and accountability.
  - Risk to researchers' careers.
  - How Referee is funded.
  - Subjectivity and disagreement.

## Talks coverage
- The Referee Project: An Update with Sebastián Buriticá Arias (2024)
  - Focus: bug-bounty-inspired review model, reliability scoring, adversarial process design, and current MVP direction.
- The Referee Project at DeSci Labs Forum (2023)
  - Focus: taking the peer out of peer review, maker/breaker role separation, transparent scoring, incentives, and AI/human review dynamics.

## Public API surface
- POST /api/newsletter
  - Purpose: newsletter subscription endpoint.
  - Request body: `email` (required), `firstName` (optional).
  - Behavior: validates input, submits double-opt-in signup request, returns JSON status/message.
